objective: Stably sort unchanged titles by standard lowercase UTF-16 keys rather than trimmed or locale-dependent alternatives.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Comparator contracts, stable sorting and nonmutating arrays remain current JavaScript/TypeScript.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Ordered labels and titles are common UI data work with an explicit ordering policy.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Key normalization, comparison units and ties transfer to other deterministic sorts.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded title strings and a three-way comparator fit the intended array lesson.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Implicit trimming or locale changes can silently reorder distinct data.

defects: Intro generalized ASCII uppercase/lowercase order to all characters.
Equal-lowercase-key ordering needed to be distinguished from broader Unicode case folding.
A comparator that trims titles before sorting passed all prior checks.
Bounded width, exact strings, fresh empty/single outputs and Unicode comparison units were unstated.
rationale: Keep all three correct stable sorts, narrow the ASCII example and define locale-independent whole-string toLowerCase then UTF-16 < and >, with no trimming, Unicode normalization or numeric/locale collation. Equal keys keep input order. Cases inspect leading/empty/space keys, non-ASCII/emoji/lone-surrogate order, dotted-I/decomposed-accent keys and1000 stable ties plus fresh mutable outputs. Target O(n log n) in the stated comparison-sort/bounded200-unit-string model; explain that unbounded strings add a length factor and language sort complexity is not guaranteed. The valid decorated-key alternative remains accepted.
